BILL NUMBER:  S4287

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and
breeding law and the tax law, in relation to the payment of certain
commissions

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To adjust the timing of payments made by the state pursuant to the
Upstate Gaming Economic Development Act of 2013 to video lottery
terminal facilities that are located in the same region as a
commercial casino so they can be made quarterly rather than annually.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Sections 1-3:  Amend section 104 of the Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering
and Breeding Law and clauses (G) and (G-2) of subparagraph (ii) of
paragraph 1 of subdivision b of section 1612 of the Tax Law to empower
the Gaming Commission to adopt, amend, and repeal a resolution to
provide that the payments made by the state pursuant to the Upstate
Gaming Economic Development Act of 2013 to video lottery terminal
facilities that are located in the same region as a commercial casino
are made quarterly rather than annually.

Section 4:Effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Current law provides for these payments to be made on an annual basis.
By adjusting the timing of these payments so they can be made
quarterly this bill will improve the financial operations of video
lottery terminal facilities without any increased cost to the state.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately, provided however that the
provisions of sections two and three of this act shall take effect on
the first day of the first quarter of the state fiscal year during
which the resolution provided for in Subdivision 24 of Section 104 of
the Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law, as amended by
section one of this act, is adopted and transmitted.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 164
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 4287-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to the payment of certain
      commissions"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Upstate New York Gaming Economic Development
Act of 2013 to provide that certain  commission  payments  made  by  the
State  to  Video  Lottery  Terminal (VLT) facilities located in the same
region as a commercial casino, are made quarterly, rather than annually.
 
  The State receives a portion of the  net  machine  income  from  video
lottery  terminals,  which  is then used to offset the cost of education
throughout the State. This bill would require the State to take  commis-
sion  payments  that  would otherwise have been made in FY 2019, and pay
them out quarterly in FY 2018. This would result in a loss  of  approxi-
mately  $24 million in education aid in FY 2018 that is not reflected in
the State's Financial Plan. Any discussions regarding the  diversion  of
funds,  especially when not accounted for in this year's financial plan,
must be addressed in the context of  the  annual  State  budget  negoti-
ations. For this reason, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
